Der Verbraucherzentrale Bundesverband ist die Stimme der Verbraucher:innen – und damit eine entscheidende Kraft in der Politik. Wir wissen, was Verbraucher:innen bewegt und verschaffen ihnen Gehör bei Politik, Wirtschaft und Verwaltung. Strukturelle Missstände decken wir auf, benennen Verbraucherprobleme und entwickeln Lösungen. So tragen wir dazu bei, dass Märkte transparent und gerecht gestaltet werden. II. Ausgangslage Zur Selbstdarstellung und zur Unterstützung der politischen Interessenvertretung veröffentlicht der Verbraucherzentrale Bundesverband regelmäßig zahlreiche Kommunikationsmaterialien. Dazu zählen Publikationen, Social-Media-Grafiken, Flyer, Visuals für Veranstaltungen und Kampagnen sowie digi- tale Formate. Im Juli 2025 wurde die neue Marke Verbraucherzentrale mit einem überarbeiteten Corporate Design eingeführt. Grundlage hierfür ist die strategische Positionierung der Marke Verbraucherzentrale. Das neue Corporate Design setzt klare und verbindliche Gestaltungsstandards für die Kommunikation und unterstützt einen einheitlichen, zeit

ung. So können auch kurzfristige oder zeitkritische Projekte zuverläs- sig umgesetzt werden. Ziel der Ausschreibung ist daher der Abschluss eines Rahmenvertrags für Grafikleistungen mit zwei Losen. Qu’est-ce que le DUME Le DUME est un formulaire électronique standardisé qui permet à un opérateur économique de présenter sa candidature à un marché public en déclarant son identité, sa situation juridique, financière et ses capacités professionnelles. Il est accessible en ligne, notamment via la plateforme https://dume.chorus -pro.gouv.fr ou directement depuis certains profils acheteurs sur https://www.marches-publics.gouv.fr. Grâce à ce formulaire, l’entreprise peut bénéficier d’un pré remplissage automatique de certaines informations à partir de son numéro SIRET, ce qui réduit le nombre de saisies. references_experience.text: (MVVM) development pattern, where you would have to code the presentation layer by creating View Models and Views for each object you wish to display, using NOF there is only a set of default generic (MVVM) views defined by NOF and they are applied to all domain objects (models). The Naked Objects pattern was first described formally in Richard Pawson's PhD thesis which includes a thorough investigation of various antecedents and inspirations for the pattern including, for example, the Morphic user interface. Naked Objects is commonly contrasted with the model-view-controller pattern. However, the published version of Pawson's thesis (see References) contains a foreword by Trygve Reenskaug, who first formulated the model-view-controller pattern, suggesting that Naked Objects is closer to the original intent of model-view-controller than many of the subsequent interpretations and implementations. Further information on the NO pattern is available at http://www.nakedobjects.org/ . Naked Objects 2.0 The BOMi currently uses version 2.0 of the Naked Objects framework, referred to as 'NOF2', which was the first publicly available framework to implement the 'naked objects pattern'. NOF2 was originally written by Naked Objects Group and supplied to the Department under an open-source licence.

When preparing a competitive quotation, vendors should take into consideration benefits provided through the national healthcare system. Quotations should refrain from over customization, and should be “off the shelf”, “commercially available”, or “market ready” products which are designed to be complementary and supplement to the national system in Portugal. The benefit levels listed from section C.1.1 through C.1.24 are a standard package that must be provided. C.1.1 Eligibility: To be eligible to participate in the medical plan, LE Staff (both full time and part time) must be: -- Paid under the terms of the Local Compensation Plan (LCP); and – -- Under a non-temporary direct hire appointment, personal services agreement (PSA), or personal services contract (PSC); or -- Under a temporary direct hire appointment or PSA Fixed Term of one year or more. Not eligible are those working under temporary appointments; those working under a PSC or PSA that is time limited to less than one year; non-personal services contract personnel and their employees, supplied by an independent contractor l

ointments; those working under a PSC or PSA that is time limited to less than one year; non-personal services contract personnel and their employees, supplied by an independent contractor licensed to do business in Portugal who provides services to other local RFP 19GE5026Q0035 – LES Health Insurance Services for U.S. Embassy Lisbon Page 6 of 21 organizations as well as to the U.S. Mission; employees working on an intermittent or When Actually Employed (WAE) schedule; Peace Corps personal services contractors and Recreation Association employees. C.1.2 Riders: There are no riders under this contract. C.1.3 Periods of Ineligibility: Employees and their dependents are not entitled to health benefits during any period of employment for which premiums are not paid. Additionally, employee's dependents are not entitled to health benefits during any period of employment during which the employee was not eligible to participate. During a period of extended Leave Without Pay (LWOP) or other unpaid leave beyond one pay period, the employee is responsible for the full cost of the insurance premiums for self and dependents. The Mission will pay the premiums directly to the Contractor and will collect the full cost from the employee on a quarterly basis. Alternatively

Over the past decade, this ecosystem has expanded organically through project ‑by‑project deployments. As a result, the current environment is characterised by fragmentation, inconsistent branding, duplication of operational and hosting costs, varied technical standards, and increasingly complex governance and content‑management structures. A preliminary mapping exercise conducted by MTA has identified more than thirty (30) digital assets, including consumer‑facing websites, corporate platforms, country‑specific domains (e.g., 14 Unclassified France, Germany, Italy, the UK, Japan, Korea, and others), MICE ‑focused portals, event ‑driven microsites, and international representative sites. These range from high ‑traffic multilingual portals such as VisitMalta.com to legacy campaign sites, temporary market blogs, outdated or abandoned domains, and internal syst

mpaign sites, temporary market blogs, outdated or abandoned domains, and internal systems supporting media management, CRM, B2B services, and training. Social media channels and API ‑based integrations further contribute to the broader content flow and technical landscape. MTA’s strategic direction is to consolidate this extensive and heterogeneous digital landscape under a unified and coherent platform centred around VisitMalta.com. The objective is to improve user experience, reinforce consistent brand representation across all markets, streamline content and technical governance, and reduce long‑term operational, maintenance, and hosting costs. To support this strategic shift, MTA requires a comprehensive Web Environment Analysis and Requirements Definition Exercise. It shall assess the current ecosystem in full, map underlying systems and content flows, identify consolidation and rationalisation opportunities, and define the technical, functional, governance, integration, and procurement requirements. The findings will directly inform the preparation of a public tender, ensuring that the future solution is robust, scalable, interoperable, secure, and aligned with MTA’s long‑term digital transformation strategy. 1.6 - Related Programmes and Donor Activities T

on and adjudication process. Ultimately, the contract will ensure that MTA has the foundations required to implement a future-proof digital platform offering consistent branding, improved user experience, enhanced operational efficiency, and strengthened international visibility. 2.2 - Specific Objectives The objectives of this contract [which are not necessarily those of the project] are as follows: 1. To carry out a complete and validated analysis of MTA’s current digital ecosystem This objective focuses on discovering, mapping, auditing, and assessing all MTA digital assets, including domains, subdomains, microsites, hosting environments, CMS platforms, integrations, 15 Unclassified SEO structures, and compliance obligations. The Consultant must identify shadow sites, legacy components, security vulnerabilities, and operational inefficiencies to establish an authoritative baseline for consolidation. The Consultant shall categorise each asset using a Retain / Migrate / Redesign / Retire model. This objective ensures that strategic, technical, functional, and governance considerations guide which elements of the current web estate are preserved, redesig ned, consolidated, or phased out. 2.
